sections.name: main
sections.title: Command entry: choosing what to run
sections.what: Reads the command options and runs either the mutation check or the eval gate. In fast mode it runs only the deterministic checks; in full mode it also runs rubric grading and the baseline comparison. It prints each result and exits with 1 if any check failed or a regression was found, otherwise 0.
sections.why: Likely reason: the exit code tells other tools, such as a build step, whether the gate passed.
sections.watch_out: If there are no golden cases, a run can still exit 0 when checks pass, so the printed warnings are the only sign that nothing was measured.

sections.title: Starting the script when run directly
sections.what: When the file is run from the command line, passes the result of the main command to the system as the exit code.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the file be imported by other code without starting the gate.
sections.watch_out: Importing this file does not run the gate; only running it directly does.

summary: The quality gate for the pipeline. It runs fast deterministic checks on golden cases, and in full mode it grades output against written rubrics. Only part of this file was in the packet.
purpose: Decides whether a pipeline change is good enough to merge, by checking shape, contracts and content, and never counting skipped checks as passes.
why: The docstring says deterministic checks show the shape is right and rubric grading shows the content is right. The two are separated by cost, so the fast one can run on every stop.
how: 1. Early sections set the result types and the folders for cases, candidates, rubrics and results. 2. Deterministic checks read each golden case's input, reference and rubric. 3. Full mode adds grading by a pinned judge model. 4. Results are saved to files and compared with a baseline. 5. A mutation section applies deliberate breakages to confirm the tests catch them. The packet names the functions run_fast, grade_case, run_mutations and main, but their code was not included.
inputs: Golden case folders with input.json, reference.md and rubric.yaml. Candidate outputs. The shared rubric YAML files. The saved baseline results file.
outputs: A report of passed, failed and skipped checks, and result files under evals/results.
risks: A run with many skipped checks can look green in the summary. The judge is a paid model call. An empty rubric file raises an unhandled error instead of a clear failure.
debug: Run the fast mode first. Each failing line names its case and check. For a skip, read the reason in the summary. For rubric problems, check that the weights sum to 1.0 and that the dimension names are known. Result files record the rubric versions and the judge model used.
